quarterly_data.signal: First billion-dollar revenue quarter: Q4 revenue surpassed $1 billion for the first time, up 20% year-over-year, with record operating profit of $226 million (21.3% margin); fiscal 2026 revenue was $3.7 billion, up 16%; Q4 product revenue of $618 million grew 25% and FY2026 product revenue of $1.97 billion grew 16% (product revenue now includes hyperscale shipments).
quarterly_data.figure: Q4 revenue > $1 billion, +20% YoY; FY2026 revenue $3.7 billion, +16%; Q4 product revenue $618 million, +25%

quarterly_data.signal: The hyperscale business grew beyond expectations in FY2026 as Pure expanded its footprint with its existing hyperscale customer; for FY2027 it expects to significantly accelerate hyperscaler shipments and revenues, with the majority recognized in Q3 and Q4 because hyperscaler revenue follows the customer's data center buildout schedule; the earlier 'low double digits' exabytes outlook for this year was confirmed and is now more than originally expected.
quarterly_data.figure: low double-digit exabytes of hyperscaler shipments (FY2027), H2-weighted

quarterly_data.signal: Standardized hyperscaler business model: Pure will procure some of the components hyperscalers need to build the solution in their environment, but not the NAND — hyperscalers continue to procure the NAND through their own supply chain — so hyperscaler revenue gross margins are expected to range between 75% to 85%, accretive to product and overall company gross margins; hyperscaler revenue sits in product revenue and is not included in RPO.

Pure is in engineering test environments at multiples of the hyperscalers with wider and broader engagement, but no second hyperscaler has been announced — 'still in the fight and not yet at the finish line', and later than expected; supply constraints are a tailwind because hyperscalers are more eager to accelerate testing and certification of new sources of supply, and a headwind to every vendor's ability to source components.

Strong component demand driven by tech-titan AI buildouts has outstripped supply across the industry, dramatically increasing NAND, memory and CPU pricing — component prices on average have more than doubled over the last 6 months; Pure raised prices on February 9 by about 20% on average (the last and lowest increase in the industry, per management) and expects Q1 product gross margins excluding hyperscaler at the lower end of the typical 65% to 70% range, recovering through the fiscal year; long-standing NAND supply agreements help mitigate but do not eliminate cost swings and potential shortages, and visibility is 'non-existent'.
quarterly_data.figure: component prices more than doubled in 6 months; price increase ~20%; Q1 product GM at low end of 65% to 70%

quarterly_data.signal: Secured the first FlashBlade//EXA customer — a GPU cloud customer standing up storage for its end customers' training and inference workloads that had initially selected an alternate vendor, ran a performance test, placed an order within days and followed with additional orders — with advanced-stage discussions underway with dozens more; EXA has achieved industry-leading MLPerf benchmark performance and the highest published SPECstorage AI Image results.
quarterly_data.figure: first FlashBlade//EXA customer (multiple sales); dozens in advanced discussions

quarterly_data.signal: FY2027 revenue guidance of $4.3 billion to $4.4 billion (18.8% growth at the midpoint) with operating profit of $780 million to $820 million; Q1 revenue guided to $990 million to $1.01 billion (approximately 28% growth) with operating profit $125 million to $135 million; 47% of FY2027 revenue is expected in H1; management says the hyperscaler business will account for a lot of the growth in fiscal year 2027, and Q4/Q1 strength is demand-based since the price increase mostly hits from Q2.
quarterly_data.figure: FY2027 revenue $4.3 billion to $4.4 billion (+18.8%); Q1 $990 million to $1.01 billion (~28%)

quarterly_data.signal: RPO growth accelerated to 40% in Q4 and ARR grew 16% to $1.9 billion; deals over $5 million grew 80% year-over-year; FY2026 capital expenditures were $264 million (approximately 7.2% of revenue), supporting data center expansion, product testing and the scaling of the hyperscale business; the company is renaming itself Everpure and agreed to acquire 1touch (1.5% dilutive to FY2027 operating profit).
quarterly_data.figure: RPO +40%; ARR $1.9 billion (+16%); deals > $5 million +80%; FY2026 capex $264 million
